summary: Initial discovery focused on CrestPoint's need for dedicated GPU capacity for low-latency customer-facing models, isolation for sensitive PII, and burst/scale behavior. Discussed tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, autoscaling/burst approaches, compliance (SOC2, KMS), and next steps for pricing and benchmarks.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood SE), David (CTO), Priya (Head of ML), Evan (Infra), Samantha (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time today. Quick intros then we'll jump into your goals for dedicated capacity.
[00:08] David: Hi, David here, CTO at CrestPoint. We're evaluating options to move production LLM workloads off multi-tenant hosted into something more predictable.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, Head of ML. We're running customer support routing and personalized responses, latency target sub-300ms for 95p on short prompts.
[00:24] Evan: Evan, infra. Primary concerns are isolation for PII, egress controls, and ability to burst during peak trading hours.
[00:32] Maya: Great, Carlos and Leah from our side will cover the technicals. Quick question on current stack?
[00:38] Priya: We're on a mix of OpenAI for some gen, and a couple of hosted open models via other providers for embeddings. Current QPS is modest, ~8 rps steady, peaks to ~50 during batch sends. Cost is creeping up, and we want predictable unit economics.
[00:55] Carlos: Got it. So sounds like Dedicated fits for predictable throughput and isolation. Curious on the burst pattern — is it short spikes or sustained increases?
[01:02] Priya: Mostly short spikes, 5-20 minutes, aligned to market opens and some scheduled campaigns. Some longer sustained loads for nightly re-ranking jobs though.
[01:12] Leah: For short bursts we often recommend a burst pool + autoscale policy: reserved baseline capacity sized for 95p steady load, and a burst headroom for short windows. That avoids huge commit costs.
[01:24] David: How does Redwood handle bursting across regions and GPUs? We have data residency needs for EU users.
[01:31] Carlos: We support region pinned Dedicated pools; you can reserve in a region and enable burst to a shared pool or to additional reserved nodes. For private/on-prem you'd get full isolation but overhead is higher. Note that our routing can fall back to a lower-cost compatible variant if capacity constrained.
[01:46] Priya: When you say "compatible variant" do you mean quantized or smaller models that still meet 95p quality? We can't have significant quality regressions for fraud detection prompts.
[01:55] Carlos: Right. In practice we recommend maintaining a primary model and a compatibility fallback with explicit quality tolerances. We run evals against your prompt set to measure delta — automatic fallback is only enabled if you opt in.
[02:07] Evan: Security: we need SOC2 type II, KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO/SAML. Is that all supported on Dedicated?
[02:15] Maya: Yes — Dedicated includes KMS integration, audit logs, RBAC, and we have SOC2 reports available. For Private deployments we can offer VPC-only control plane and on-prem for air-gapped setups.
[02:26] Samantha: Procurement question: what's the minimum commit and contract length? Also any termination/overage terms for burst usage?
[02:33] Maya: Minimums vary, typically quarterly commitments for Dedicated, with monthly or annual pricing. Burst can be configured as paid usage above reserved or as pre-provisioned burst pool. We'll send the template and pricing in follow-up.
[02:44] David: Performance — can you share typical tail latency numbers for the family of models? Our 95p goal is strict.
[02:50] Carlos: For short seq lengths (<=128 tokens) on our Gpu-80 class, 95p latencies are around 120-200ms for most quantized open models, and ~80-120ms for optimized Redwood-verified variants. But this depends on sequence length and KV cache behavior.
[03:08] Priya: What's the impact of batching? We need low latency per request but also cost pressure.
[03:13] Leah: Dynamic batching helps throughput but can add ms of waiting; our serving runtime supports continuous batching with latency SLOs and workload-aware batching rules. You can tune batch windows (e.g., 5ms) to trade a few ms for lower token cost.
[03:25] Priya: Ok. Also curious about stateful workloads — we have a lot of session KV cache usage for chat histories. How do you manage cache footprint and eviction?
[03:33] Carlos: We have KV cache management and per-instance cache sizing. For Dedicated you can configure larger KV caches per node and we recommend sticky routing to preserve caches for active sessions. There are TTLs and eviction policies we can tune.
[03:46] Evan: On networking, we need private connectivity and control plane separation — can Dedicated be VPC peered?
[03:52] Maya: Yes, Dedicated can be deployed with private peering options; for full control plane separation we'd discuss a Private deployment. Many customers start on Dedicated with VPC peering and then move to Private for regulatory needs.
[04:04] Samantha: Any references for banks or regulated customers doing dedicated?
[04:08] Maya: We can share redacted case studies; I'll attach a one-pager and SOC2 artifact.
[04:12] David: On cost modeling — if we reserve 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs, how do we estimate tokens/sec and concurrency?
[04:19] Carlos: It depends on model, seq length, and quantization. As a rough guide, a single A100-eq on our runtime for quantized LLM 7B-ish gives ~25-40 RPS for short prompts; 4 GPUs with batching and autoscale can handle concurrency with headroom. We'll run a replay with your prompts to produce a sizing recommendation.
[04:35] Priya: We also need to understand cold start and scaling cooldowns — we can't have 30s times when scaling up.
[04:41] Leah: Our autoscaler supports pre-warm and staged rollout for new nodes. Burst pool is often used so that cold start happens in a smaller pool while baseline waits. There is a tradeoff with cost.
[04:53] David: Licensing / data retention: do logs or customer data persist in shared services?
[04:59] Maya: By default we retain audit logs per account; you can configure retention or forward logs to your SIEM. Data in transit and at rest is encrypted; with Dedicated you get isolation and with Private you can keep logs on your side.
[05:12] Priya: Any limitations around custom kernels or model code? We use some custom ops.
[05:18] Carlos: Dedicated supports customer-supplied model artifacts in many cases; custom kernels need validation but we have an onboarding path. For Private on-prem we can be more flexible.
[05:27] Samantha: Procurement follow-up — do you accept PO? Payment terms?
[05:31] Maya: Yes, enterprise customers can use PO and net terms; we'll include standard terms in the pricing doc.
[05:36] David: Great. Can you summarize recommended next steps?
[05:40] Maya: Sure — we'll send pricing options for 2/4/8 GPU reserved pools, region choices, and burst configurations. Carlos will prepare a benchmark plan and we'll need your prompt set and traffic trace. Then we schedule a replay benchmark.
[05:54] Priya: Sounds good. Also please include an evaluation of fallback model quality — we won't accept >2% regression on our intent classification.
[06:02] Carlos: We'll run automatic evals and report quality deltas per prompt set; can include per-prompt thresholds.
[06:09] David: Cool. Anything else?
[06:12] Evan: Just to confirm, can we do initial onboarding into EU region only?
[06:15] Maya: Yes, region pinning is supported. We'll note that in the pricing.
[06:20] Samantha: I'll expect the pricing doc and SOC2 link by Friday.
[06:23] Maya: We'll get that over. Thanks everyone.

[06:30] Meeting recap (rough): Need dedicated baseline sized for 8 rps steady / 50 rps peaks; burst pool for 5-20 minute spikes; region pinning to EU; SOC2/KMS/audit logs required; next steps: pricing, prompt set, benchmark replay.

Notes on transcript quality: some words auto-transcribed (e.g. "KV cache" as "K V cache", "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes "Redwood Dedicate"). Occasional crosstalk and filler words removed for clarity.

References shared: pricing template (link placeholder), SOC2 report (link placeholder), benchmark replay instructions (link placeholder).

End of transcript.
